module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 839

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/839](https://www.erdosproblems.com/839)
- [Er78f] Erdős, P., *Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on
  Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).

See also [Erdős Problem 359](https://www.erdosproblems.com/359) and
[Erdős Problem 867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real Finset
open scoped ENNReal

namespace Erdos839

/-- A sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is "sum-of-consecutive-free" if no term equals
the sum of a contiguous block of earlier terms. That is, for all $i$,
$a_i \neq a_j + a_{j+1} + \cdots + a_k$ for any $j \leq k < i$. -/
def SumOfConsecutiveFree (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, ∀ j k : ℕ, j ≤ k → k < i →
    a i ≠ ∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc j k, a l

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 1) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\limsup a_n / n = \infty$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ≥0∞) / n) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 2, stronger) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log x} \sum_{a_n < x} \frac{1}{a_n} = 0$?

This is equivalent to asking whether the range $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}$ has logarithmic density zero
(see `Set.HasLogDensity`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    Set.HasLogDensity (Set.range a) 0 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Formalize the additional material on the possible lower limit, reciprocal-sum growth,
-- upper-density constructions, and the links with Erdős Problems 359 and 867.

end Erdos839

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a zero-indexed sequence and an ENNReal-valued quotient a n / n. In particular, its n = 0 quotient is infinity, whereas the source indexes the sequence from 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Reindex the source sequence by b_(n+1) = a n; positivity, strict increase, and the consecutive-block condition are preserved. For n ≥ 1, a n / (n+1) ≤ a n / n ≤ 2 · (a n / (n+1)), so either sequence of ratios has infinite limsup exactly when the other does. ENNReal agrees with ordinary nonnegative real division for these positive denominators, and its complete-lattice limsup is the usual extended limsup. The single infinite initial value is irrelevant to limsup atTop; this finite-initial-term invariance was checked in Lean, though the complete reindexing equivalence was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses Set.HasLogDensity (Set.range a) 0, whose definition takes natural cutoffs and sums over values k ≤ n, rather than the source’s real cutoff x and sum over sequence terms a_n < x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: StrictMono makes a injective, so summing over its range counts each sequence term exactly once. At a natural cutoff n, inclusive and strict sums differ only by the possible endpoint contribution 1/(n log n), which tends to zero. Natural and real strict-cutoff limits are equivalent: write the latter sum using the integer cutoff ceil(x), and for x ≥ 2 bound its normalized value between zero and twice the normalized sum at ceil(x); the reverse implication follows by restricting to integer x. The scratch lemma part_ii_equivalence proves the full equivalence between HasLogDensity of the range and the real-cutoff, sequence-indexed formula, assuming StrictMono a, without using sorry axioms.
